history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTIFICATION NOTE: this is NOT the famous Siddheshwar Temple at Solapur (CSV seq 614, dedicated to the 12th-century Lingayat saint Siddharameshwar). The 'Shri Siddheshwar Maharaj Temple' listed under Aurangabad most plausibly refers to the temple/samadhi shrine of a different Hindu mystic, Sant Siddheshwar Maharaj, at Dhotra village in Sillod taluka of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district (PIN 431112). Hindu-blog records an annual Siddheshwar Maharaj Yatra at Dhotra in the month of Magh, dedicated to the saint, with special puja and abhishek and an evening palkhi procession attracting thousands of followers; a video documents the samadhi centenary (shatabdi) celebration held at Dhotra in 2014. There is also a 'Shree Sidheshwar Maharaj Sansthan' at Babra Road, Phulambri (~32 km from Aurangabad city), a spiritual organisation with a Siddheshwar idol that may or may not be related (verify which shrine the CSV row intends). No detailed published biography of the Dhotra saint was found; do not conflate him with Shri Siddharameshwar Maharaj (1888-1936, guru of Nisargadatta Maharaj) or with the Solapur saint. A separate well-documented Siddheshwar Mahadev temple complex exists at Kayegaon Toka (Ahmednagar, near the Godavari-Pravara confluence; ASI documents a 1767 reconstruction) - also a different shrine.

name: Shri Siddheshwar Maharaj Temple
town_description: Aurangabad (officially Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, is a major historic city known as the 'City of Gates', with the Bibi Ka Maqbara, Daulatabad Fort, and the nearby Ajanta and Ellora UNESCO World Heritage cave complexes. The Siddheshwar Maharaj shrine identified here is not in the city itself but at Dhotra village in Sillod taluka, roughly 50 km northwest of the city on the Sillod/Ajanta side (verify distance).

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Airport (approx. 50-60 km from Dhotra; taxis available) (verify distance).
travel.railway: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Railway Station (approx. 50-60 km from Dhotra; nearest local stations at Sillod/Palod) (verify distance).
travel.road: Dhotra village, Sillod taluka, PIN 431112; reached by road via Sillod from Aurangabad city (Aurangabad-Ajanta/Sillod road, near MH SH 8). Public and private buses run on the Aurangabad-Sillod corridor; exact public transport to the shrine is not published (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. The annual Siddheshwar Maharaj Yatra in Magh month (roughly January-March; e.g. 2027 yatra date around early March per Hindu-blog) is the most significant time but draws large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not reliably published online (verify - village samadhi shrines typically open early morning to evening; confirm locally before visiting). No entry fee expected.
